_meta.name: ETF Holdings Pension Funded Ratio Trajectory Dataset
_meta.purpose: 5-year per-employer CalPERS / CalSTRS / county-system funded-ratio histories for ETF muni holdings (K-12 USDs, successor RDAs, state/county GO, water districts). Feeds detectors/pension_funded_ratio_trajectory.py for trajectory-based exclusion.
data_sources_primary: CalPERS Public Agency Actuarial Valuation Reports (per-employer-plan, annual). Index: https://www.calpers.ca.gov/page/employers/actuarial-services/employer-contributions
CalSTRS Defined Benefit Program Actuarial Valuation Reports (systemwide, annual). https://www.calstrs.com/general-information/actuarial-valuations-and-reports
SDCERA Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (San Diego County independent system). https://www.sdcera.org/about/financial-reports
GASB 68 disclosures embedded in employer audited financial statements (ACFR)
California State CAFR pension footnote (CalPERS state-plan tier)
_meta.data_quality_caveat: CalSTRS publishes a SYSTEMWIDE funded ratio; per-school-district disaggregation is NOT available (each district participates pro-rata in the statewide DB plan). For K-12 districts the 5-year history shown is therefore the systemwide CalSTRS DB ratio — district variation is captured via GASB 68 net-pension-liability-to-revenue multiples in the per-obligor _notes. CalPERS publishes PER-EMPLOYER reports (Misc + Safety pools separately). Where individual employer reports were not directly retrieved in this session, we use the systemwide CalPERS Public Agency funded ratio with confidence='MEDIUM' and flag for primary-source pull.

confidence_legend.HIGH: Per-employer CalPERS or independent-system report URL cited with FY-specific ratio
confidence_legend.MEDIUM: Systemwide CalPERS/CalSTRS ratio used as proxy; per-employer report not retrieved this session
confidence_legend.LOW: Single-point estimate or staff-disclosed figure without retrieved primary source

hostile_validator_notes: CalSTRS systemwide history is the PUBLIC ratio (76.7% as of June 30 2024 per CalSTRS 2024 funding-plan report cited in ca_pob_universe.json fact_7). Pre-2024 systemwide history pulled from CalSTRS public disclosures.
CalPERS systemwide Public Agency funded ratio history: 75% (FY2024), 71.4% (FY2023), per ca_pob_universe.json fact_7. Earlier years are CalPERS plan-wide self-disclosure.

Per-employer CalPERS Misc/Safety reports require manual PDF retrieval per employer per year. Where this session uses systemwide ratio as proxy, that is flagged confidence=MEDIUM and the per-obligor verdict notes 'PROXY' explicitly.
SDCERA is INDEPENDENT (NOT CalPERS) — San Diego County employers including the County itself participate in SDCERA, not CalPERS. SDCERA 2024 funded ratio ~78% per ACFR.

K-12 ETF holdings (River Delta USD, Alpine USD, etc.) have ZERO per-district CalSTRS exposure separability — the funded ratio used is systemwide. The trajectory therefore reflects systemwide pressure, not district-specific underfunding.

San Jose Successor RDA._notes: San Jose is OUTSIDE CalPERS — runs own Federated + Police & Fire plans (per ca_pob_universe.json line 281). Federated plan has been chronically underfunded (50s%) for >10 years. Trajectory: 53 -> 58 = +5pp (improving) but LEVEL still <60% = CRITICAL — fires HIGH on snapshot floor. RDA successor agency's debt service is secured by property-tax increment trapped in the Redevelopment Property Tax Trust Fund (RPTTF) which is SHIELDED from host-city pension claims. So while the city pension situation is bad, the structural masking via RPTTF means signal may not propagate to successor-RDA bond price the way snapshot suggests. Hostile-validator caveat: detector fires, but masking mechanism (RPTTF intercept) may compress alpha.

_verdict_summary.structural_caveat: RPTTF intercept (Successor RDA debt service paid out of property-tax-increment trust trapped by County Auditor-Controller) MASKS host-city pension distress from RDA bondholders. San Jose Successor RDA fire is therefore a partial-credit signal — the cash-flow mechanism for the bonds is insulated from city general fund. Detector fires; price impact likely compressed by mask. This pattern parallels CSFA LCFF intercept for charter schools and dedicated-tax statutory lien for K-12 GO.
_verdict_summary.k12_caveat: CalSTRS systemwide funded ratio improved 67.1 -> 76.7 over the 5-year window covered (FY2020 -> FY2024). This is anti-correlated with the Stockton/Vallejo-era pattern (where CalPERS was declining). No K-12 ETF holding will fire on this systemwide trajectory. To flag district-specific pension stress, the detector needs GASB 68 net-pension-liability / governmental-fund-revenue multiples by district (current detector data file does not include this — open gap).
_verdict_summary.sacramento_usd_reference: Sacramento City USD was the load-bearing CalSTRS-stress reference in the task spec; it is NOT in the ETF-holdings list provided. The April 2026 Fitch BB- cut on Sacramento USD was driven by ESSER cliff + enrollment loss + general-fund deficit, not CalSTRS systemwide funded ratio (which improved over the same window). This is itself a microstructure finding: CalSTRS systemwide trajectory is too coarse to flag district-level distress; pension contribution rates (set systemwide) hit weak districts disproportionately but the trajectory metric is uniform.
